post_copy:
The Air Force offered federal land for AI data centers. The pause Fairbanks North Star Borough asked for can't reach a foot of it.

Resolution 2026-25 sets 25 priorities, 21 state and 4 federal. One heading appears on both lists. It asks for a moratorium on new commercial data centers on state-owned or municipal lands.

Twelve parcels were on offer at three installations. Only Eielson is in this borough. Responses closed May 29th.

Presiding Officer Scott Crass told KUAC by phone that federal land was intended too. The text adopted on August 27th says state or municipal lands.

The heading printed twice, the seven standards it waits on, the twelve parcels and the property line between them.

One sentence, two governments. Which copy does the work, the one whose words fit its target or the one whose intent does?

#DataCenterSiting #AlaskaLegislature #InteriorAlaska

The words say state land.The intent was wider.
Presiding Officer Scott Crass told KUAC by phone that federal land was meant to be included too. The text adopted on August 27th doesn't say that, and both lists carry the same words.
An ask is the wholepower a borough has here.
Mayor Grier Hopkins said the community wants to know how data centers can best be regulated and "where, if anywhere, should we put them in our community." No standard exists yet for any of the seven.
Which of the seven should Alaska write a standard for first?

editor_notes_for_email: The caption ships byte for byte from the room and no factual error was found in it, so nothing was touched. The deck's central object is a constructed diagram of survey markers, one per item on the adopted list, and slides 1 and 7 say exactly that in a mono legend, because a reader who takes it for a photograph of a real site is this deck's main misreading risk. If the post underperforms, watch the swipe from slide 1 to slide 2, since the cover poses a counting question and the payoff sits entirely on the second card. Slide 6 was rebuilt late in the run: its body used to reprint the five dates its own numbered chips carry, which made it the deck's heaviest frame and, in two independent flow reads, the place a reader stops. It now carries two sentences and hands the turn forward, and the day rail runs off the right edge unterminated so the swipe into slide 7 has somewhere to go. The likeliest correction request is the May 29th response deadline, because a third party mirror and an older docket entry say June 29th, and the sam.gov record itself reads 2026-05-29 with an archive date of June 13th and an empty award object. Second likeliest is the land wording, since both outlets printed state-owned AND municipal while the resolution's own text reads OR, which is why slide 7 and the caption both write or. All three claims that were dropped in the first build are now carried. C04, the sponsor line, is back in slide 2's body. C27, the single installation bid clause, is back in slide 5's body. C08, the stamped heading, is struck into both tag faces on slide 8, which is also what makes that slide's two stamps provably the same object. Before pasting, read the first comment back once, because the two borough clerk links carry parentheses and a comma inside the URL and a mangled paste kills the primary document.
aftercare: Post this in a Tuesday to Thursday window, 8 to 11am Alaska time, one slot only. Drafts land daily and the cadence is yours.
Paste the sources comment within 60 seconds of posting, before the first impressions land.
Read the pasted comment back once and confirm the two civicclerk links survived with their parentheses and commas intact.
Stay in the thread for the first 90 minutes and reply to every comment, including the one word ones.
Answer the deck's own question first with a real pick from the seven, which is what makes the ask read as open rather than rhetorical.
Corrections outrank everything. If a reader says the federal deadline moved, the sam.gov record as read this run says responses closed May 29th, 2026 and the docket carries the dated correction.
Leave the post alone after the first hour. An edit resets distribution and buys nothing.
Note saves, comments and swipe depth at 48 hours and write them into the run record.
